title: 446 - Touchdown Fever
method: sample: written by Claude Code from the transcript, links verified by script

items.name: Touchdown Fever
items.description: The episode's game: SNK's 1987 arcade football title, ported to Famicom in 1988 and the NES in February 1991.

links.label: Touchdown Fever (NES) - The Cutting Room Floor

items.name: SNK
items.description: Developer and publisher of Touchdown Fever, which arrived too late to compete with Tecmo Bowl.

items.name: 10-Yard Fight
items.description: Irem's 1985 football game, the bar Touchdown Fever is compared against.

items.name: Irem
items.description: Made 10-Yard Fight, the earlier football game the hosts compare this one to.

links.label: Wikipedia: Irem
links.note: Japanese video game and pachinko company

items.name: Tecmo Bowl
items.description: The 1987 arcade football hit that SNK had to compete with, praised for adding strategy.

items.name: Tecmo
items.description: Publisher of Tecmo Bowl, whose rosters and play-calling set the standard Touchdown Fever ignores.

items.name: Super Tecmo Bowl
items.description: The next football game the hosts look forward to covering.

items.name: John Elway's Quarterback
items.description: An earlier NES football game that Mike says Touchdown Fever's scale looks nothing like.

items.name: Ice Hockey
items.description: The early NES hockey game Joe says Touchdown Fever reminds him of, with its chibi-style players.

items.name: Blades of Steel
items.description: Joe's first guess for the hockey game he was thinking of before correcting himself.

items.name: NFL Blitz
items.description: The arcade game the hosts play at the Long Island Retro Game Fest, which Joe says doesn't interest him.

items.name: Madden NFL
items.description: Joe's example of the kind of football game with play-picking he doesn't enjoy.

items.name: Family Computer (Famicom)
items.description: Japan's version of the NES, which got Touchdown Fever American Football in 1988.

items.name: Chain Chomp
items.description: Joe's joke when the box's tagline mentions "the chomp": the Mario enemy, not a football term.

items.name: Scorigami
items.description: The idea of a final score that has never happened in NFL history; Mike notes 31-5 has happened before.

items.name: Two-point conversion
items.description: A rule Touchdown Fever includes before the NFL adopted it.

links.label: Wikipedia: Two-point conversion
links.note: Play in American and Canadian football

items.name: Lateral pass
items.description: The odd mechanic of tossing the ball sideways after a forward pass, which the game leans on.

links.label: Wikipedia: Lateral pass
links.note: Type of short pass in football

items.name: National Football League
items.description: The league Touchdown Fever lacks a license for, so it uses generic city teams.

items.name: Buffalo Bills
items.description: Mike and Sean's team, undefeated when the episode was recorded.

links.label: Wikipedia: Buffalo Bills
links.note: NFL team in Orchard Park, New York

items.name: Josh Allen
items.description: The Bills quarterback Sean had a prop bet on.

items.name: Houston Texans
items.description: The Bills' opponent in their first game, won 28 to 17.

items.name: Detroit Lions
items.description: The Bills played them on Thursday night; Sean also played as Detroit and saw the lion mascot.

items.name: Arizona Cardinals
items.description: Beat the Texans 31-5 four years ago, which closes the door on the Scorigami joke.

items.name: Patrick Mahomes
items.description: Mentioned as the Chiefs quarterback in the failed attempt to end the episode on a positive.

items.name: Travis Kelce
items.description: Sean finds the Kelce and Taylor Swift coverage insufferable.

items.name: Taylor Swift
items.description: Paired with Travis Kelce in the closing banter.

items.name: NEStalgia Essential Games List
items.description: Where each host's verdict on the episode's game is collected; Touchdown Fever was a no.
